pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the drumhead do when it is struck? (1 mark)
   A. It stays completely still
   B. It vibrates and makes the sound
   C. It cools the drum
   D. It holds the drum stand

2. How is a kayamba played? (1 mark)
   A. By shaking it
   B. By rubbing a bow across it
   C. By plucking strings
   D. By blowing into it

3. Which player mainly tries to stop the shooter? (1 mark)
   A. GK
   B. GS
   C. C
   D. WA

4. Macramé is a technique of (1 mark)
   A. tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   B. carving wood
   C. painting on cloth
   D. beating drums

5. What should you do after passing the ball? (1 mark)
   A. Close your eyes
   B. Walk off the court
   C. Move into space to receive it again
   D. Sit down

6. Where must a player stand to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. Anywhere on the court
   B. Behind the goal post
   C. At the centre circle
   D. Inside the goal circle

7. What do you add to a colour to make it darker? (1 mark)
   A. Black
   B. Yellow
   C. White
   D. Water only

8. A slab of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a round ball
   B. a hollow cup
   C. a thin roll
   D. a flat piece

9. The bottom stripe of the Kenyan flag is (1 mark)
   A. black
   B. white
   C. green
   D. red

10. In a crab balance, your tummy faces (1 mark)
   A. down
   B. sideways
   C. up
   D. backwards

11. In a crab balance, what is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Straight arms
   B. Head in line
   C. Hips lifted
   D. Hips sagging near the mat

12. In a side roll, your body should be (1 mark)
   A. hanging in the air
   B. curled like a ball
   C. bent at the waist
   D. straight and long like a log

13. Gestures in singing are (1 mark)
   A. hand and body movements that fit the song
   B. quiet time
   C. words only
   D. sounds of the drum

14. Tempo means (1 mark)
   A. how loud the music is
   B. the name of the song
   C. the speed of the music
   D. the number of verses

15. Funeral songs are usually (1 mark)
   A. about sports
   B. fast and joyful
   C. loud only
   D. slow and sad

16. When photographing a child, it is good to (1 mark)
   A. bend down to their eye level
   B. photograph from above only
   C. shout
   D. stand on a chair

17. Photography is (1 mark)
   A. singing songs
   B. cutting paper
   C. the art of taking pictures with a camera
   D. painting with a brush

18. Who should you ask before using a school digital device? (1 mark)
   A. A teacher or adult
   B. Nobody
   C. A friend's pet
   D. A stranger

19. The song Hot Cross Buns can be played on (1 mark)
   A. only G and C
   B. B A G
   C. only drums
   D. C D E only

20. What should you do before playing to prevent spreading germs? (1 mark)
   A. Chew gum
   B. Share the recorder
   C. Eat sweets
   D. Wash your hands

21. Where should a recorder be stored? (1 mark)
   A. On a hot windowsill
   B. In the mud
   C. Under a heavy load
   D. In its bag or box

22. Where should the mouthpiece rest? (1 mark)
   A. On your chin
   B. Between your lips, not your teeth
   C. Between your teeth
   D. Behind your ear

23. In the sit-and-slide entry, you first (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. jump
   C. dive
   D. sit on the edge with feet in the water

24. Which is part of pool hygiene? (1 mark)
   A. Wearing dirty clothes
   B. Not passing urine or spitting in the pool
   C. Not showering
   D. Eating in the pool

25. Prone means (1 mark)
   A. face up
   B. face down
   C. standing
   D. sitting

26. What helps your body to float? (1 mark)
   A. Holding a stone
   B. Kicking hard only
   C. Being heavy
   D. Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air

27. In a supine float, you lie (1 mark)
   A. on your back with ears in the water
   B. face down
   C. curled up
   D. standing

28. A hare hop suits a rhythm that is (1 mark)
   A. silent
   B. very slow
   C. quick like ta-te ta-te
   D. absent

29. In the frog jump, you should land (1 mark)
   A. on your back
   B. on your head
   C. softly with bent knees
   D. stiff

30. In a folk song, the soloist (1 mark)
   A. plays the drum only
   B. leads and sings the call
   C. is the audience
   D. is silent

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Where do the notes B, A and G sit on the staff? (3 marks)

32. Give the French rhythm names for a crotchet and a pair of quavers. (2 marks)

33. Explain how you decide whether a percussion instrument is melodic or non-melodic. (3 marks)

34. What is stepwise motion? Give an example. (2 marks)

35. Give four safety rules for animal games. (4 marks)

36. Explain why covering more holes makes a lower note. (3 marks)

37. Describe how to make a value scale strip of orange. (3 marks)

38. How should you give feedback on a friend's photograph? (3 marks)

39. Describe how to blow to make a good tone. (3 marks)

40. Describe how to do the frog jump. (3 marks)

41. Name three water games and say how one is played. (3 marks)

42. Compose a four-beat rhythmic pattern using a crotchet, a pair of quavers and a rest, and write it in rhythm names. (4 marks)

43. Give four ways in which gymnastics helps the body. (4 marks)

44. Describe how to do the mushroom float. (3 marks)

45. Why is light important in photography? (2 marks)

46. Why do we improvise a netball? (3 marks)

47. Why should you collect only dead or fallen twigs for charcoal? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — It vibrates and makes the sound
   The stretched skin shakes very fast and produces sound.

2. A — By shaking it
   The kayamba is a shaker with seeds inside. You shake it back and forth.

3. A — GK
   The Goal Keeper guards the goal and defends against the shooter.

4. A — tying knots to make patterns and shapes
   Macramé is done by tying cords in knots.

5. C — Move into space to receive it again
   Moving into open space keeps the game flowing.

6. D — Inside the goal circle
   Shots must be taken from inside the goal circle.

7. A — Black
   Black makes a shade, a darker tone.

8. D — a flat piece
   A slab is a flat sheet of clay.

9. C — green
   Green is at the bottom.

10. C — up
   The tummy faces the ceiling like a table top.

11. D — Hips sagging near the mat
   Hips should stay lifted to make the body level.

12. D — straight and long like a log
   A straight, tight body rolls smoothly.

13. A — hand and body movements that fit the song
   Gestures help tell the story of a song.

14. C — the speed of the music
   Tempo is how fast or slow.

15. D — slow and sad
   They comfort families and remember the person.

16. A — bend down to their eye level
   Eye level gives a friendly picture.

17. C — the art of taking pictures with a camera
   A photograph is a picture taken by a camera.

18. A — A teacher or adult
   Always get permission.

19. B — B A G
   It uses the three notes B, A and G.

20. D — Wash your hands
   Clean hands help hygiene.

21. D — In its bag or box
   A case protects it.

22. B — Between your lips, not your teeth
   Lips form the seal.

23. D — sit on the edge with feet in the water
   You sit, turn and slide in.

24. B — Not passing urine or spitting in the pool
   Keeping the pool clean matters.

25. B — face down
   Prone is face down.

26. D — Water pushes up on it and lungs full of air
   Buoyancy and air in the lungs.

27. A — on your back with ears in the water
   You look at the sky.

28. C — quick like ta-te ta-te
   Hares hop quickly.

29. C — softly with bent knees
   Bent knees absorb the shock.

30. B — leads and sings the call
   The soloist starts or leads.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: B is on line 3, A is in the space between line 2 and line 3, and G is on line 2.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Crotchet: taa. Pair of quavers: ta-te.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the sounds. If it plays different notes, high and low, that make a tune, it is melodic. If it gives only a beat or one kind of sound, it is non-melodic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for melodic meaning, 1 mark for non-melodic meaning.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Moving from a note to the next note above or below. For example, d to r.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Play on soft, clear ground; warm up; keep a distance from others; do not push or trip; drink water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: The column of air inside becomes longer, and a longer air column vibrates more slowly, giving a lower note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for longer air column, 2 marks for lower note.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw a strip and divide it into five boxes. Mix orange with white for the two light boxes. Paint pure orange in the middle. Mix orange with black for the two dark boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the five boxes, 1 mark for light tones, 1 mark for dark tones.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Say what you like first, comment on light and centre of interest, and suggest one improvement politely.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the mouthpiece between the lips, take a deep breath, blow gently and steadily, and start each note with a soft too or doo.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Squat with hands on the ground. Spring forward with the legs. Land softly on toes and hands with bent knees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bubble blowing, treasure hunt, follow the leader, water tag, circle walk. One correct explanation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for three games, or 1 mark each for two games and an explanation.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example taa ta-te (rest) taa. Any four-beat pattern with all three parts and ending on a crotchet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for four beats, 1 mark for using all three, 1 mark for correct names, 1 mark for ending on a long note.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Makes muscles stronger; improves flexibility; improves balance and coordination; exercises the heart and lungs; builds confidence. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: In shallow water take a breath and put the face in. Bend the knees and hug them to the chest with the chin tucked. The back rises to the surface. Hold for a few seconds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Light lets the camera record the picture. With good light the subject is clear.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Some schools do not have enough balls. We can use materials we have, such as string and waste cloth. It lets more learners practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: To protect the environment and living trees. Dead twigs are also dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for protecting living trees, 1 mark for the environment or dry wood.
